proposals.title: Once braking for a detected lead has begun, keep demand applied until own speed reaches zero
proposals.trigger: A lead target is present in the range channel, own speed is above zero, and at least one brake command has already been issued for this episode.
procedure: Check own speed, not the gap, as the progress measure: the episode's terminal success is certified by own speed reaching exactly zero with a non-negative gap, so a stable, positive, non-growing gap is not an end state.

While own speed is above zero, never return to hold; issue the demand that brings own speed to zero inside the current range reading rather than the smallest demand that merely decelerates. Own speed falls monotonically even under a demand too light to avoid contact, so "raise it if own speed stops falling" would never fire in time.

If the previous decision returned zero acceleration and an unchanged own speed while a brake demand was outstanding, that is the normal three-tick actuation lag, not a released command: wait one more decision before changing demand.
Only stop applying demand once own speed reads exactly zero at the end of a decision; at that point the collision-avoidance predicate is satisfiable.
successSignals: final decision still issues a brake command while own speed is zero
brake demand is never reset to hold across the run once deceleration has started
own speed decreases monotonically to zero with the gap non-negative throughout
failureSignals: own speed plateaus at a nonzero constant with zero acceleration and zero brake demand
gap remains positive and roughly constant while own speed stays above zero
episode ends by decision_budget_exhausted with no contact recorded
recovery: As soon as a plateau in own speed at nonzero is observed, immediately re-apply brake demand rather than holding through further decisions.
invariants: success requires own speed at or below the target's with the gap never reaching zero; outside CCRb a standstill is not required.

proposals.title: A newly filled or newly frozen observation reopens the decision instead of repeating hold
proposals.trigger: Either the range/rangeRate channel that read empty on previous decisions has become finite, or the last several decisions have returned identical own speed and identical range while own speed remains above zero.
procedure: Compare the current reading with the previous one before selecting an action; a channel that has just gained a value is a new decision point, not a continuation.

On the first decision with a finite range and a closing rate, compute the closing geometry from the reading already in hand and issue brake demand at that same decision rather than waiting for a further reading.

When consecutive decisions show own speed and range unchanged, stop treating the freeze as an absence of threat — the frozen state means your last command is still in force and the decision budget is being spent without progress; act.
Do not spend decisions accumulating additional identical readings before committing; the reading in hand is sufficient to choose.
successSignals: brake demand is issued on the first decision after the range channel becomes finite
no run of identical own-speed and range readings occurs while own speed is above zero
failureSignals: hold is repeated across decisions before and after the range channel fills
several consecutive decisions reproduce the same own speed, range and acceleration with no demand applied
recovery: On detecting a plateau, treat it as a deadline: apply brake demand on the next decision and re-evaluate immediately afterwards.
invariants: holding is a choice to keep the previous command in force, not a passive wait
an unchanged observation with zero acceleration and zero demand implies the ego is coasting and nothing will change on its own

proposals.title: The early-onset advisory labels an action, it does not fail the episode
proposals.trigger: You are choosing between holding and braking, the computed time-to-collision is above the threshold the task instructions describe as nuisance braking, and the scenario still requires the ego to come to rest.
procedure: Prefer committing to at least a light brake demand over holding when the standstill predicate is still unreached, whatever the stated onset threshold says.

Treat the nuisance-braking label as a recorded attribute of the run, not as a loss condition: a recorded success of this bench carried that label at onset and still reached the terminal standstill with full score.
Weigh the two failure modes explicitly — braking somewhat earlier than the advisory prefers is recoverable; running out of decision budget while still moving is not.
Size the demand from the gap and the closing rate, not from the label: the nuisance flag never costs score, and contact is the only failure branch, so never trade stopping margin for a cleaner onset.
successSignals: episode terminates with own speed zero even though the recorded brake onset was labelled nuisance braking
a light, sustained demand carries the ego to a standstill
failureSignals: no brake demand is ever applied while own speed remains high
episode ends by budget exhaustion with nuisanceBraking reported false and the ego still moving
recovery: If decisions are being consumed without a standstill and no brake has been applied, apply a light demand immediately rather than continuing to hold for a cleaner onset.
invariants: a false nuisance flag coincides with never stopping; a true nuisance flag coincides with a scored success in this bench
the onset threshold governs labelling only, not the terminal outcome
